meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Switzerland (federal sovereign jurisdiction; cantonal commercial registries operate as delegates of the federal Commercial Register Authority)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (codified Swiss-German/French mixed tradition based on the Civil Code (ZGB) and Code of Obligations (OR); no binding common-law precedent doctrine)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Art. 620-763 Swiss Code of Obligations (OR/CO, SR 220) for the Aktiengesellschaft (AG); Art. 685i-685w OR (register of registered shareholders and 25% disclosure threshold); Art. 626 para 2 no. 1 and Art. 621 OR (statutory seat and minimum capital of CHF 100,000 with CHF 50,000 paid-in); Art. 632c OR (blocked-account capital deposit requirement). AML/CFT: Federal Act on the Prevention of Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLA/GwG, SR 954.0) of 10 October 1997, as amended to 1 January 2023 (including crypto-asset service providers); FINMA Anti-Money Laundering Ordinance (AMLO-FINMA, SR 955.033.0). UBO transparency: Federal Act on the Transparency of Legal Entities and the Identification of Beneficial Owners (TJB law, SR 221.536) of 22 June 2023 (phased entry into force; non-public central register; 25% threshold). Sanctions: Federal Embargo Act and SECO sanctions ordinances (SR 946.2 series); Swiss Criminal Code Art. 305bis and 305ter (money laundering and lack of financial due diligence).

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory onboarding and continuous real-time screening of all founders, directors, authorized signatories and UBOs against the UN Security Council Consolidated Lists, Swiss SECO Embargo Register, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions Lists, OFAC SDN/SSI Lists, UK OFSI Consolidated List and FINMA public enforcement register. PEP status is determined per Art. 2a para 1 AMLO-FINMA and the Swiss Bankers Association Guidelines (SBA-GIN 2023); enhanced due diligence (EDD) is triggered by PEP status, high-risk jurisdiction indicators or crypto-asset payment exposure. Screening results are documented in the KYC/beneficial-ownership file maintained by the incorporating fiduciary and are subject to Swiss data-protection and bank-secrecy rules.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix - Central Business Name Index (https://www.zefix.ch); the pre-incorporation name reservation is filed electronically via the eHR/sofia application system of the competent Cantonal Commercial Registry Office (e.g., Handelsregister des Kantons Zug for the Crypto Valley seat)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Pursuant to Art. 950-954 OR, the corporate name must respect the principles of civic liberty and informational truthfulness, be expressed in Latin script in one of the Swiss official languages (German, French or Italian), and include the mandatory legal-form suffix 'AG' (Aktiengesellschaft). English names are generally admissible if they pass the truthfulness test, but Chinese-character names are not registered until a recognized Latin-script transliteration in a Swiss official language is added. The name must not suggest a public-law character, banking, insurance, or licensed regulated activity without prior authorization.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Finance / Finanzgruppe (FINMA-licensed terms under Art. 31 AMLA and Banking Act Art. 3)
Insurance / Assurance / Versicherung (requires FINMA license under Insurance Supervision Act Art. 2)
Trust / Fiducia / Fiduciary (restricted; requires fiduciary-license and cantonal authorization where applicable)
Payment / Payment Services / Zahlungsdienst (requires FinSA/FinIA authorization where applicable)
Eidgenossenschaft / Confederation / Bund / Swiss National Bank (reserved federal terms requiring SECO consent under Art. 954a OR and Firmenverordnung)
Asset Management (requires FINMA license under FinIA/CISA where investment management is implied)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation may be extended once for an additional 90 days upon written application to the Cantonal Commercial Registry Office (Art. 14 para 2 HRegV). If the proposed name is rejected, the applicant may file an administrative objection with the Cantonal Supervisory Authority (Oberaufsichtskommission) within 10 days of the rejection notice; a subsequent appeal lies to the Civil Division of the Federal Administrative Court (Bundesverwaltungsgericht) within 30 days. A Zefix negative pre-check does not constitute a legally binding decision, and a fresh application with a revised name may be submitted without prejudice.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices and registered-agent models are accepted by the cantonal commercial registers for an AG only when combined with a physically occupied Swiss business address, a Swiss-resident director or local authorized signatory, and a substantive service agreement with a licensed fiduciary. A pure post-office box is rejected in most cantons. For a license-free crypto tax SaaS (ISIC 6201) seated in Zug, a serviced office or co-working address with fiduciary administration is market practice and satisfies the rebuttable-presumption of commercial substance under Swiss federal direct tax law (Art. 50, 58, 61-62 DBG) and the OECD/EU substance rules.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate: estimated 5-10% annual probability of an unannounced physical inspection for a low-risk, license-free software company; announced substance reviews by the cantonal tax administration and ESTV occur typically every 3-5 years, with increased scrutiny observed in the Zug crypto cluster since 2023 but concentrated in licensed financial intermediaries, not pure software-as-a-service business models.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (OR, SR 220), Articles 620 to 763 (Aktiengesellschaft / Stock Corporation), notably Articles 626 to 632 and 643 to 647 concerning incorporation, share capital, paid-up capital, and board representation; Federal Act on the Amendment of the Swiss Civil Code, Part Five.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt / Greffe du commerce) of the canton of the registered office, operating under the federal framework supervised by the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certified Deed of Incorporation and Articles of Association (Statuten), accompanied by the official commercial register application form R040/A for legal entity registration (Anmeldung zur Eintragung in das Handelsregister).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum issued share capital for a Swiss AG is CHF 100,000. At incorporation, at least 20% of the nominal capital (CHF 20,000) must be paid in, but in any case no less than CHF 50,000 must be paid in cash and deposited into a blocked Swiss bank escrow account (Sperrkonto). The bank must issue written blocking confirmation before notarisation; the escrow release only after commercial register registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: the incorporation deed and articles of association are approved, and the founders' subscription to the company's Swiss franc share capital is accepted; RESOLVED: the registered office is fixed at the stated address in the canton of the Commercial Register entry, and the Articles shall be filed for registration under the Swiss Code of Obligations; RESOLVED: [Name] (Chairperson) and [Name] (Chief Executive Officer, sole signatory) are appointed as officers and vested with single-signature authority; RESOLVED: the officers are authorised to execute the commercial register application, operate escrow accounts, and take all ancillary acts; RESOLVED: all acts already performed in the company's name are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Escrow and Notarisation of Incorporation Deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss notary public in the canton of the registered office, acting with the chosen Swiss bank holding the blocked escrow account.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked incorporation escrow account under the future company name (Sperrkonto) and deposit at least CHF 50,000 in cash. Obtain the bank's blocking confirmation and draft the articles of association. Attend a notarial authentication session, where the incorporators declare the subscription of CHF 100,000 share capital, adopt the articles, and approve any contribution-in-kind report if applicable.
required_dossiers: Valid passports or identity cards of all incorporators and board members
Draft Articles of Association (Statuten)
Branches of bank blocking confirmation for CHF 50,000 minimum paid-up capital
Proof of physical premises or registered office consent from the landlord/municipality
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary issues a query, correct the deficient statutory clauses and resubmit for a second notarial appointment. Founders may also elect to increase or adjust share premium to cure capital payment defects before signing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) of the chosen Swiss canton.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the R040/A application electronically or in paper form, together with the notarised deed, certified articles of association, identification of directors and authorised signatories, specimen signatures, and proof of capital blocking. Pay the cantonal registration fee and await substantive review.
required_dossiers: Completed R040/A registration form
Notarised deed of incorporation
Certified copy of Articles of Association
Identity documents and signature specimens of board members
Bank blocking confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a preliminary rejection, remedy the stated legal deficiencies by filing an amended declaration or supplementary documentation within the statutory deadline. If the articles are rejected on substantive grounds, convene an extraordinary general meeting to adopt conforming amendments.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: SHAB Publication and Allocation of Swiss Business Identifier
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB) and Swiss Federal Statistical Office through the Commercial Register authority.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: No separate filing is required; after registration, the Commercial Register Office transmits the data to SHAB for statutory publication and to the central UID register for automatic issuance of the Federal Business Identifier (UID). Verify the published SHAB entry and UID allocation within statutory timeframes.
required_dossiers: Commercial register extract proving date of entry
UID online access registration details (EBICS or UID portal)
SHAB publication confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SHAB publication contains errors, request a correction filing with the Commercial Register Office and, where appropriate, an official correction notice in SHAB. For delayed UID, contact the Central UID Service to obtain the formal UID confirmation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: VAT, Employer, and Federal Social Security Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA) through the VAT Quarterly or Single Window, and the Cantonal Compensation Fund (AHV/IV/EO) plus SUVA or an approved accident insurer.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register for VAT with the Federal Tax Administration if taxable turnover from crypto tax software services, licences, or SaaS subscriptions is expected to exceed CHF 100,000 per year. Register as an employer with the cantonal compensation office for old age, survivors' and invalidity insurance (AHV/IV/EO), and arrange compulsory accident insurance before hiring staff.
required_dossiers: UID number and commercial register extract
Articles of association and board member identification
Expected turnover estimate for software licences and online services
Bank details for federal tax collection
Planned employee payroll information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If VAT registration is queried, correct the economic activity code to ISIC 6201 and submit revised projected turnover figures. Retroactive registration can be requested by filing a supplementary disclosure to the ESTV. For AHV/IV/EO, coordinate with the canton to issue a corrected employer entry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Cantonal Business Permit and Work Premises Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Department of Economic Affairs and Labour (Amt für Wirtschaft und Arbeit) together with the municipal trade licensing and building inspectorate authorities.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a cantonal/municipal business operation declaration or obtain a Gewerbebewilligung where required by cantonal law for commercial offices. Complete the building occupancy and fire safety clearance for the registered office, and confirm occupational health compliance under Swiss Labour Law. Physical inspections may be required once staff occupy premises.
required_dossiers: Commercial register extract and UID
Lease agreement or building tenancy documentation
Municipal building occupancy permit or construction acceptance if applicable
Fire safety clearance certificate
Employer workplace registration with the cantonal labour inspectorate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If municipal authorities impose deficiency notices, remedy fire safety, building load, or workstation deficiencies and submit an occupancy attestation. If the permit is denied, appeal to the cantonal administrative court within 30 days of notification.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Cantonal Department of Economic Affairs and Labour (Amt für Wirtschaft und Arbeit / Office de l'économie et du travail) and municipal trade licensing office in the registered municipality.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Cantonal/Municipal Business Operation and Workplace Clearance (Betriebsbewilligung / Gewerbebewilligung)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN/BAFU) and the competent cantonal environmental protection agency (Amt für Umwelt)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration/Exempt for ISIC 6201 digital asset tax software activity; no full EIA report or prior environmental impact assessment permit required for office-based software operations with no industrial installation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC emission thresholds apply to administrative software offices; compliance required with the Federal Act on the Protection of the Environment (USG), the VOC Ordinance (SR 814.018) for any printing equipment, and the Waste Ordinance (SR 814.600) for electronic equipment disposal. Domestic sanitary wastewater discharges through municipal sewage must meet communal discharge permits. Any HVAC refrigerants must comply with the Ozone-Depleting Substances Ordinance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The premises require a municipal fire safety certificate, a structural load and building occupancy approval from the local inspectorate, and workplace health clearance under Art. 6 and Art. 16 of the Swiss Labour Law, including first-aid readiness, evacuation planning, and electrical equipment inspection. Occupational accident prevention and workplace ergonomic compliance are supervised by SUVA or the cantonal labour inspectorate.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung / Administration fédérale des contributions, ESTV/AFC) for Swiss VAT and federal direct tax withholding; cantonal and communal tax administrations for corporate income and capital tax registration; centralized online portal 'ePortal ESTV' (TaxMe) at https://eportal.estv.admin.ch, plus the Federal Statistical Office UID portal (Central Business Name Index 'Zentraler Firmenindex').
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-incorporated entity with Swiss indirect-tax nexus must first obtain a Swiss UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer) via the federal UID portal; VAT registration then proceeds through the ESTV ePortal using the 'Registration/Adjustment for VAT-liable persons' form (MWST/TVA). The Swiss AG (CH_AG) obtains its UID automatically upon commercial-register entry in the canton of incorporation and receives a separate MWST-Nr. (VAT ID) when VAT registration is perfected. Non-resident shareholders may hold 100% of the share capital and exercise full control. A company without Swiss commercial-register entry but performing taxable activities in Switzerland must complete the ePortal non-resident registration flow, designate a Swiss notification address/electronic service domicile, and will by default file on a six-month settlement or annual reporting basis.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Switzerland does not provide US-style 'check-the-box' pass-through elections; an AG is mandatorily subject to entity-level taxation at federal, cantonal and communal levels. Available statutory elections include: (i) the small-business VAT exemption election where worldwide turnover is below CHF 100,000 and turnover excluding real-estate services is below CHF 250,000; (ii) optional ordinary group taxation (effective 1 January 2025) allowing a financially integrated group to elect aggregate tax-unit treatment, and the special tax-status group regime for financial institutions; (iii) cantonal tax elections for patent box/QRD deductions and equity-reduction allocation. Hybrid mismatch elections are not available; Switzerland follows the OECD hybrid mismatch design within its GAAR framework, which must be respected in the crypto tax-accounting product logic.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 annual worldwide turnover from non-exempt supplies (Art. 10 VAT Act); non-resident suppliers making supplies used or performed in Switzerland are also liable at the CHF 100,000 threshold, with certain services supplied by non-residents to Swiss recipients subject to reverse-charge transfer of liability below that threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland does not impose real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or mandatory API reporting to tax authorities. A VAT invoice must contain the vendor's VAT number and Swiss UID, transaction and invoice dates, sequential invoice number, supplier and recipient identity, nature and quantity of supplies, tax rate, tax amount, and total amount. B2B e-invoicing commonly uses the SIX 'Paynet' and Swiss QR-Bill (Swico/Swiss Implementation Recommendations) interchange formats. Foreign and domestic suppliers must retain complete invoicing records; the ESTV does not provide fiscal pre-encryption APIs, but the crypto tax SaaS must document the CHF reference or the foreign-currency conversion method on every invoice for audit integrity.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported by the CH_AG qualify for the 0% Swiss VAT rate where the goods physically leave Switzerland and the dispatch is conclusively evidenced. Services, including SaaS/cloud-based crypto-tax calculation and bookkeeping software, qualify for 0% when the recipient has its place of business/effective seat abroad and the service is economically used or beneficially enjoyed outside Switzerland, and the service is not for a Swiss permanent establishment of the foreign recipient. The commercial model must document the foreign subscriber's residency and the absence of Swiss in-country benefit to sustain zero-rating.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (Swiss export declaration/SED, or NCTS declaration where required by customs procedure)
Bill of lading, air waybill, or equivalent transport document evidencing physical dispatch outside Switzerland
Inward remittance certificate or payment-track evidence showing settlement by the foreign buyer (including USDC on-chain payment verification where applicable)
Commercial invoice compliant with Art. 27(3) VAT Act
Export-transaction ledger reconciling e-invoicing data to the customs declaration
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ESTV subjects software exporters, including crypto-SaaS platforms, to heightened audit scrutiny on zero-rating claims. If export or foreign-benefit evidence is defective, the 0% treatment is retrospectively reversed, VAT is reassessed at the standard 8.1% rate, and default interest of 5% per annum runs from the original invoice due date. Administrative fines for tax contraventions (such as incomplete invoice data) amount ordinarily to up to CHF 8,000; intentional tax evasion triggers penalties up to three times the evaded tax and criminal proceedings under VAT Act Arts. 57-60 and 47. Repeated or flagrant zero-rating misuse can additionally result in retrospective revocation of the VAT registration and the imposition of security obligations for future liabilities under Art. 55 VAT Act.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB) / Schweizerische Nationalbank, acting in coordination with the Federal Department of Finance (FDF), the State Secretariat for International Financial Matters (SIF), and the Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland operates a full convertibility regime grounded in constitutional economic freedom (Art. 27 Federal Constitution) and adherence to the OECD Capital Liberalisation Code. Both capital and current account transactions are liberalized; no exchange control authorization, mandatory licensing, or central bank approval is required for cross-border payments, capital injections, or profit repatriation applicable to a Swiss Aktiengesellschaft. The Swiss franc (CHF) is a freely floating, fully convertible reserve currency. Software export and SaaS subscription revenues may be invoiced and retained in USD, EUR, or USDC without restriction. Profit remittance (dividends, royalties, licence fees) is unrestricted from an FX perspective; the only fiscal friction is the Swiss 35% anticipatory withholding tax on dividends, which is refundable for Swiss-resident recipients or reduced under the applicable US-Swiss double taxation treaty (typically 0% for qualifying corporate shareholders holding substantial participation and 15% otherwise), and which does not constitute a currency control hurdle. There is no exchange-rate approval, no compulsory repatriation, and no surrender-of-export-proceeds requirement for a Swiss corporate treasury.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory export proceeds surrender rules in Swiss law. The SNB imposes neither a mandatory conversion ratio nor a statutory repatriation timeline for export receipts or cross-border service income. A Swiss AG may hold 100% of its foreign-currency export proceeds (USD, EUR, or stablecoin) indefinitely in non-CHF accounts. The only indirect obligation is statistical: banks participating in the Swiss Payment Convention (SPC) must report cross-border payment instructions with structured remittance information for SNB balance-of-payments and direct-investment statistics; this requires the company to designate correct ISO 20022 purpose codes (e.g., EQUI for equity injection, SUPP for supplier payments, ROYA for royalties) and to respond to the SNB's annual direct-investment survey where material cross-border positions exist.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account + multi-currency treasury line (CHF/USD/EUR) with FX and hedging desk
Operational Account / Capital Escrow Account; digital-asset-friendly corporate banking unit
Digital asset custodial and operational account for fiat-crypto (USDC) conversion and stablecoin treasury
Operational Account (secondary cash concentration and domestic disbursement)
Operational Account (payroll, vendor, and domestic SIC clearing)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-Medium. EU Electronic Money Institution authorisations do not passport into Switzerland; Swiss law requires a FINMA banking licence or the Swiss innovation (fintech) banking licence under Art. 1b Banking Ordinance for public deposit-taking above CHF 100 million. Offshore digital EMIs (EU or UK-based platforms such as Revolut Business or Wise) cannot act as the primary deposit-taking treasury counterparty for a Swiss AG and are frequently de-risked by Swiss core banks when listed as sole beneficiary of inbound capital injections. Reasonable deployment is as auxiliary payment rails: a regulated Swiss fintech processor for Stripe settlement and USDC fiat off-ramping integrated with a tier-1 Swiss bank anchor account. Legal constraints include Swiss AMLA counterparty due-diligence, FIDLEG-Go/FINSA classification if the company provides payment-related services, and contractual data protection rules (nFADP) on client financial data transfer to non-Swiss processors.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical attendance is de facto mandatory for corporate account opening where the ultimate beneficial owners and at least one authorised signatory (CEO or CFO) are non-Swiss residents and the underlying business model carries a digital-asset nexus. Swiss tier-1 banks implement a two-stage verification: (1) preliminary screening via video-ident, notarised constitutional documents, and corporate register extraction; (2) an in-person interview at the bank branch or before a Swiss notary/regulated fiduciary for the ultimate beneficial owner and board-delegated signatory. Remote-only account opening is not realistically available for a US-parented crypto tax-accounting SaaS; the operational baseline is a one-day executive visit to Zurich or Geneva. A registered Swiss office address with a regulated fiduciary, a signed Swiss Economic Interest Declaration (Steuerdomizil), and the proving of a valid Swiss VAT/UID number are prerequisites. Directors who are not signatories need not appear physically, provided the authorised signatory covers the interview and the board passes a validated signing-minutes resolution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Crypto business nexus triggering automatic de-risking by compliance committees (on-chain revenue, USDC receivables)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: FINMA confirmation or qualified negative declaration that no VASP licence is required for non-custodial SaaS; audited Swiss AMLA-compliant anti-money-laundering policy with a named money-laundering officer; audited financial statements evidencing no client-money touching; product documentation isolating the tax-calculation and bookkeeping engine from any transfer/custody function; bank-specific digital-assets sector questionnaire completed with wallet-address registry and transaction monitoring controls.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Stablecoin (USDC) revenue conversion flagged as potential money laundering or unlicensed payment activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Circle USDC attestation reports and issuer licence documentation; whitelist of FINMA-recognised fiat on/off-ramps; signed perpetual compliance agreement with a licensed Swiss financial intermediary (Sygnum or AMINA) for stablecoin-to-CHF conversion; source-of-funds declarations and on-chain forensic reports for all initial USDC balances; documented commercial rationale proving stablecoin receipt arises solely from SaaS subscription payments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership opacity and cross-border parent-subsidiary structure (US-owned AG)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Swiss commercial register extract with registered-share capital structure; notarised beneficial ownership declaration under Swiss AMLA Art. 4; constitutional documents with registered share-only clause; passport copies, address history, and tax-identification numbers of all UBOs with voting power above 25%; bank reference letter from the US parent's relationship bank on SWIFT RMA letterhead; board resolution on the CHF 100,000 minimum capitalisation with liberational proof.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and high-risk jurisdiction exposure embedded in global SaaS reseller distribution network
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed AML/ATF addenda with every reseller and distribution partner; daily sanctions-screening logs exported from an automated screening solution (e.g., ComplyAdvantage or KYC360); tenant-level geo-blocking evidence for OFAC/EU and SECO-embargoed territories; annual independent AML/ATF audit report by a SECO-recognised auditor with findings-addressed opinion; no-embedded-device declaration covering the software's export classification under Swiss SECO.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity injection from the US parent to CH_AG is executed via SWIFT MT103/TT, credited to the UBS or ZKB CHF operational account with ISO 20022 purpose code 'EQUI' (Equity Investment). The Swiss Payment Convention requires the instructing bank to embed structured remittance information and beneficiary reference data so that SNB balance-of-payments statistics are populated automatically. The onboarding bank verifies the capital injection against the notarised capital-call resolution and the audited liberational statement; CHF 100,000 minimum authorised share capital under Art. 621 OR with at least CHF 50,000 paid-in cash on registered shares per Art. 632 OR must be evidenced before the account receives third-party funds. The US parent must procure a source-of-funds letter, SWIFT RMA key activation, and a K-turnaround ticket confirming the cleared funds; the receiving Swiss bank applies no FX surrender or conversion mandate, allowing the capital to be parked in CHF or temporarily in USD at the company's election, subject only to negative-interest provisions historically applied by Swiss institutions (currently neutral to slightly positive policy rates).
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary outbound clearing rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 for cross-border SaaS supplier, vendor, and parent-service payments with ISO 20022 purpose codes (SUPP for services, ROYA for royalties, DIVI for dividend distributions subject to 35% anticipatory tax retention or treaty-reduced rate); (2) SIC (Swiss Interbank Clearing) for domestic CHF payroll, VAT (MWST), and operational disbursements; (3) SEPA Credit Transfer via PostFinance or ZKB for euro-area operating costs; (4) Commercial Letter of Credit (SWIFT MT700) reserved for physical hardware resellers or enterprise implementation contracts requiring trade-finance instruments; (5) CLS-settled spot and forward FX operations for USD/CHF and EUR/CHF interbank conversion where a UBS/CLS membership tier is accessible. All outbound instructions must carry the beneficiary LEI (or registered address for non-LEI entities), complete ERI remittance reference, and the applicable Swiss Accounting-FIFO/RECOM purpose descriptor to avoid payment screening delays. Liquidity concentration is structured around a zero-balancing overlay: ZKB operates as the main distribution hub, UBS as the FX and liquidity bridge, and Sygnum/AMINA as the USDC-to-CHF conversion gateway; intraday liquidity is swept under a Swiss cash-pooling agreement with interest-compensation clauses.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX Forwards (USD/CHF, EUR/CHF) with UBS, ZKB, or BCV under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with Credit Support Annex and Swiss-law-governed confirmation terms

Cash-settled Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) restricted to exotic liquidity corridors (e.g., emerging-market software-reseller currencies) where local deliverability is legally constrained; CHF- and EUR/CHF-referenced NDFs are operationally unnecessary given the deep liquid forwards market in Switzerland and are avoided for regulatory-capital efficiency
Cross-Currency Swaps (FXS / CCS) for long-dated USD/CHF balance-sheet hedging, collateralised via SIX SIS repo parking or Swiss money-market eligible collateral

Vanilla FX Options (EUR/CHF calls/puts and USD/CHF risk reversals) permitted where the company maintains a margining account and posts collateral under the ISDA CSA; all derivatives must satisfy the business-purpose (hedging-only) test under Swiss accounting law and are documented to avoid any FINMA dealer-licensing threshold; the SNB/FINMA framework imposes no product prohibition or mandatory exchange-clearing requirement for corporate end-users hedging permitted current-account exposures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM) approval of annual accounts, discharge of the Board of Directors, and profit appropriation resolution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' meeting (internal corporate decision; minutes retained at registered office; only register-relevant changes, e.g., director changes, are filed with the Cantonal Commercial Register Office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the balance-sheet date (31 December fiscal year-end: AGM by 30 June; calendar disclosed in the Commercial Gazette if convened late)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct state filing penalty; failure to convene within six months permits a shareholder or creditor to request the court to convene the meeting (Art. 699 CO); persistent default places director survival at risk and may trigger a Commercial Register dissolution inquiry, but does not directly cause strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Combined cantonal and Swiss federal corporate income and net-wealth tax return (Tax on Profit plus cantonal Equity Tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal tax administration (e.g., Zug Steuerverwaltung), acting as collecting agent for the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Typically 3–6 months after fiscal year-end; calendar-year companies are generally assessed between March and June of the following year, with extensions routinely granted upon written request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest at 4.5% p.a.; final-reminder default assessment; administrative penalty of 10–30% of evaded tax or fine up to CHF 10,000 for intentional or grossly negligent violation; unpaid assessed tax is enforced through Swiss debt-collection and potential bankruptcy, not administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual report and audited financial statements submission to the Commercial Register (mandatory for companies subject to ordinary statutory audit; voluntary op-in for smaller companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Handelsregisteramt (Cantonal Commercial Register Office) with publication of the applicable particulars in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the balance-sheet date (31 December fiscal year-end: submission by 30 June)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative warning followed by monetary fine up to CHF 5,000 under Art. 325bis StGB and potential Commercial Register compliance audit; repeated failure to comply may culminate in court-ordered dissolution and strike-off proceedings under Art. 152–153 ORC.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual wage and payroll declaration for social insurance (AHV/AVS, ALV, BVG contribution statements and occupational pension balances)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: OASI/AVS compensation office (Ausgleichskasse) and registered BVG pension foundations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual wage statement for the preceding calendar year due by 31 January of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Surcharge of 1–5% on late or underpaid contributions; default interest at 5% p.a.; intentional misdeclaration constitutes criminal tax fraud; debts enforced by debt collection with no administrative strike-off consequence.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary (full) audit: exceeds 2 of 3 thresholds for 2 consecutive years – total assets at least CHF 10 million, revenues at least CHF 20 million, average headcount at least 250, plus mandatory for listed or regulated entities. Limited (simplified) audit: exceeds 2 of 3 thresholds – total assets at least CHF 500,000, revenues at least CHF 1 million, average headcount at least 10. Micro-entities below limited thresholds may fully waive audit by unanimous shareholder consent; any shareholder holding at least 10% may demand at least a limited audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (Art. 957–963b) applied as Swiss GAAP FER; IFRS permitted for listed companies and used by selected large holdings; crypto-asset and digital-token balances recognized at fair value under Swiss GAAP FER practice and reviewed annually by the statutory auditor.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The AG must maintain a beneficial-owner register (Art. 697j–697l CO) listing every individual holding at least 25% of capital or voting rights; the register is verified and confirmed in writing at each Annual General Meeting; ownership transfers between record dates must be promptly recorded; the register is not filed annually with the state but must be shown to the Commercial Register and auditors upon request; failure to maintain or truthfully update it is a criminal offense under Art. 325bis StGB (fines up to CHF 100,000) and exposes directors to personal liability and Commercial Register enforcement action.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Share certificate and share transfer ledger (if certificated shares issued)
Minutes book of shareholders' general meetings and board meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350–1,700 (CHF 300–1,500) per year; Zug Crypto Valley registered-office premium up to USD 2,300 (CHF 2,000) per year
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,800–9,500 (CHF 2,500–8,000) for a Swiss limited audit; USD 0 if the unanimous shareholder audit waiver applies for micro-entities; ordinary full audit for larger SaaS entities typically USD 15,000 and above

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal direct corporate income tax at 8.5% of net taxable profit plus cantonal and communal profit taxes; combined effective headline rate ranges from approximately 11.5% to 21.0% depending on the canton of residence of the Swiss AG.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general federal statutory tax holiday applies. Cantonal tax holidays of up to 10 years may be granted for newly established enterprises of particular economic interest at the discretion of the canton. Preferential income tax measures include the patent/IP box, which exempts up to 90% of qualifying patent income, and cantonal research and development super-deductions of up to 150% of qualifying R&D expenditure in certain cantons. For a crypto tax accounting SaaS undertaking, ordinary software subscription income is not patent-box income unless a separately qualifying patented technology is exploited.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Steuererklärung für juristische Personen / Déclaration fiscale pour personnes morales filed electronically through the cantonal e-tax portal and transmitted to the Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/AFC). No separate federal form is issued; the combined cantonal/federal corporate income tax return is the sole annual return for a Swiss AG.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The corporate income tax return is due within six months after the statutory fiscal year-end, subject to cantonal extension. For a calendar-year filer this normally means 30 June of the following year. Any balance of tax assessed becomes payable within 30 days of the assessment notice.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal entity identification: commercial name, registered seat, Swiss UID and VAT number, statutory company purpose, date of incorporation, and identity of shareholders.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident taxpaying entity must identify the Swiss permanent establishment or branch registration, provide the Swiss UID for the PE, and state the foreign head-office tax residence and applicable DTA article.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting basis: fiscal year end, balance sheet date, accounting principles applied, and reporting currency.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident branches must file in Swiss francs and convert foreign-currency items using the Federal Tax Administration exchange rates for the tax year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement of taxable income: operating revenue from crypto tax SaaS subscriptions, digital asset accounting fees, consulting income, royalties, interest, and other ancillary income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Swiss-source income attributable to the Swiss PE or Swiss-situs assets. Foreign-source income is excluded if a DTA assigns the profit to the foreign residence state and no PE is created.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Expenses and profit adjustments: deductible operating costs, depreciation, staff costs, third-party fees, arm's-length intercompany charges, and add-back of non-deductible items such as tax penalties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany charges from the foreign head office must comply with the arm's-length standard; unsubstantiated management fees and interest are recharacterised as constructive dividends.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions and reliefs: loss carryforward set-off, participation exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains, patent/IP box deduction, R&D super-deduction, and any notional interest deduction allowed by the canton.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use losses only if they can be evidenced from Swiss books and records and are within the seven-year carryforward limit. Treaty non-discrimination provisions do not broaden loss availability for a foreign-controlled PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Equity capital and net worth declaration for cantonal capital tax: share capital, reserves, retained earnings, and hidden reserves represented by accumulated profit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The PE must allocate its equity capital based on the functions, assets, and risks of the Swiss PE; Swiss capital tax applies to the PE share of net taxable capital.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers cantonal procedural penalties and default interest on unpaid tax. Failure to file after a formal reminder can result in estimated assessment and an administrative fine of up to CHF 10,000. Intentionally incorrect filing constitutes tax evasion punishable by a fine of up to three times the tax evaded; tax fraud through falsified books carries a monetary penalty of up to CHF 250,000 and/or imprisonment of up to three years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% Swiss federal withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) applies to dividends distributed by a Swiss AG to shareholders, including foreign corporate and individual shareholders. Cantonal and communal withholding taxes do not apply to dividends.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A non-resident shareholder qualifying under an applicable double taxation agreement must submit Form 822 to the Federal Tax Administration within the statutory application period, generally three years after the end of the calendar year in which the dividend was paid. The application must attach an official tax residence certificate (TRC) from the home jurisdiction, evidence of beneficial ownership of the shares, shareholding threshold compliance, and confirmation that the shareholder is not treaty-shopping. For Swiss-parented groups, the Swiss payer may apply for relief at source using the simplified objective form procedure if the qualifying parent holds the required participation and the DTA grants an exemption or reduction.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid by a Swiss AG to a non-resident are not subject to Swiss statutory withholding tax; however, under most DTA protocols royalty income is usually taxable only in the residence state, with Switzerland retaining no source tax. Interest payments are subject to 35% Swiss withholding tax when they constitute securities or bank deposit interest; treaty rates for arm's-length interest are generally reduced to 0%, provided the beneficial owner is resident in the treaty state and no excess-interest element exists. Royalty and interest payments must be documented for transfer pricing purposes.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Swiss law imposes no general mandatory Local File or Master File threshold based solely on entity size; however, the Federal Tax Administration expects contemporaneous transfer pricing evidence upon request for any material related-party transaction. For practical compliance, a Local File is advisable for aggregate related-party cross-border transactions exceeding CHF 1 million, and a Master File is recommended for multinational groups with consolidated revenue above CHF 50 million. Country-by-Country Reporting is mandatory for groups with consolidated revenue of CHF 900 million or more.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Offshore-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) of zero-tax jurisdictions do not apply to Switzerland. Nevertheless, Swiss constitutional and treaty practice requires every Swiss AG to have genuine business substance at its registered seat and place of effective management: physical offices, qualified staff, board meetings, independent decision-making, and real economic activity. A crypto tax SaaS company must employ actual technical, compliance, and development functions within Switzerland. Where substance is absent, tax authorities may ignore the Swiss entity, deny treaty benefits, recharacterise revenue as belonging to the foreign parent, and expose the structure to BEPS and exchange-of-information scrutiny.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally understating taxable revenue from digital asset accounting subscriptions, fabricating expenditure records, omitting gains from crypto treasury assets, or submitting materially false financial statements to the cantonal tax administration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax evasion is punishable by an administrative fine of up to three times the tax evaded. Tax fraud committed by falsification of vouchers or books carries a monetary penalty of up to CHF 250,000 and imprisonment of up to three years. The underpaid tax itself remains collectible with default interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The chief executive and financial officers are individually indictable as the organs responsible for filing accuracy; upon conviction they face imprisonment, criminal fines, civil damages under Article 754 of the Swiss Code of Obligations, and travel restrictions during criminal investigation. A court may order restitution of the evaded tax from personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends, making economic benefits available, or paying interest covered by Swiss withholding tax to a non-resident without deducting the 35% tax, or claiming DTA relief without a valid tax residence certificate and beneficial ownership proof.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Swiss AG becomes liable for the full withholding tax, statutory interest, and recovery costs. In aggravated cases, the concealment of one's tax-collection obligation constitutes tax fraud punishable by a fine of up to CHF 250,000 and/or imprisonment of up to three years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Withholding obligations are imposed on the company's organs; directors who knowingly cause the company to pay dividends without withholding can be personally assessed with the tax and interest. The Swiss tax authority may impose a travel ban and initiate asset seizure where there is a risk that the funds will be moved abroad without payment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a Swiss AG with no real staff, offices, client contracts, decision-making, or bookkeeping activity; routing intangible services and crypto revenues through Switzerland solely to obtain a lower combined tax rate or treaty benefits, while actual management remains abroad.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority may disregard the Swiss entity, reallocate profits to the actual economic owner, impose a constructive dividend at the recipient level, and apply 35% withholding tax on deemed distributions. The AG may thereafter be reported to the commercial register for bankruptcy or involuntary dissolution if it cannot demonstrate ongoing business activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held civilly liable for damages caused to the company and tax authorities by being a mere mailbox entity; willful violation of substance requirements is treated as a sham arrangement and may support a finding of criminal fraud, leading to personal restitution, travel bans, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting USDC or other crypto-currency subscription payments without maintaining adequate customer and beneficial-owner identification, monitoring transactions for sanctions exposure, or refusing to co-operate with financial intelligence units when the platform is used as a conduit for proceeds of tax evasion or fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Although the software entity is not automatically a supervised financial intermediary under the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act, acts of providing financial services or facilitating cryptocurrency payments may trigger FINMA oversight. Violations can lead to administrative fines, confiscation of digital assets, and criminal penalties under the Swiss Criminal Code (Art. 305bis and 305ter), including imprisonment of up to three years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who knows or should know that crypto subscriptions are being used to launder tax fraud proceeds may be prosecuted as an accessory to money laundering. Conviction results in imprisonment, monetary penalty, confiscation of proceeds, travel bans, and disqualification from holding director positions; personal civil liability is available to affected creditors and state authorities.
